title: Arbitrary base change and coherence of the nodal graph cone
statement:
Let $f:X\to T$ be a flat locally finitely presented morphism of schemes such that every nonempty geometric fibre is equidimensional of dimension one and every nonsmooth geometric fibre point has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field. Put $D=\operatorname{Sing}(f)$, the first-Fitting singular subscheme, with inclusion $i:D\hookrightarrow X$. For every morphism $a:T'\to T$, put $f':X\times_TT'\to T'$ and identify $D'=\operatorname{Sing}(f')=D\times_TT'$ by [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular]. Let $a_D:D'\to D$ be the projection and let $\mathcal G_f,\mathcal G_{f'}$ be the graph conormal algebras of [lem-sfb-graph-cone-gluing]. The canonical graph-ideal comparison is an isomorphism
$$c_a:a_D^*\mathcal G_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G_{f'}.$$
On affine graph neighbourhoods it is the map $[b]\otimes r\mapsto[b\otimes r]$ on ideal-power quotients. On the pullbacks of a nodal chart its coordinate expression for every $A$-algebra $A'$ is
$$A'\otimes_AA[u,v]/(uv)\longrightarrow A'[u,v]/(uv),\quad r\otimes u\mapsto ru,\quad r\otimes v\mapsto rv.$$
It identifies the degree-zero basis and the bases $u^n,v^n$ in all positive degrees. For composable $a:T'\to T$, $b:T''\to T'$ one has $c_{a\circ b}=c_b\circ b_D^*c_a$ under canonical tensor associativity, and $c_{1_T}$ is the identity. These comparisons are natural under isomorphisms of families. They induce canonical isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{Proj}_{D'}\mathcal G_{f'}\xrightarrow{\sim}(\operatorname{Proj}_D\mathcal G_f)\times_DD'$$
compatible with the structural maps, identity base changes, compositions and family isomorphisms. No flatness is required of $a$. Here tensor pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback], fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product], and relative Proj is [def-nagata-relative-proj]. Flatness, local finite presentation, geometric fibres, pure dimension, smoothness, completion and power series are [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-pure-dimension], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The singular subscheme is [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme].

proof.text: Flatness and local finite presentation of $f'$ follow respectively from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. For an algebraically closed field $\Omega\to T'$, the geometric fibre of $f'$ is the geometric fibre of $f$ at the composite $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus the pure-dimension and completed-node hypotheses hold for $f'$ too. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] to identify $D'=D\times_TT'$ scheme-theoretically. In particular this identification allows nonreduced singular schemes.

On an affine graph neighbourhood $Y=U\times_VD_U$, with closed graph ideal $J$, its base change along $a_D$ is the corresponding graph neighbourhood for $f'$. Apply the existence clause of [lem-pur-conormal-algebra-flat-base-change], without its flatness hypothesis, to this Cartesian square of closed graphs. It gives the graded algebra map $[q]\otimes r\mapsto[q\otimes r]$ on the ideal-power quotients. These maps commute with restriction: both orders send the representative $q$ to its restricted pullback and multiply by the restricted coefficient $r$. The restriction identifications of [lem-sfb-graph-cone-gluing] therefore identify the local maps on affine refinements of overlaps. They glue to $c_a:a_D^*\mathcal G_f\to\mathcal G_{f'}$. Its degree-zero map is the canonical identification with $\mathcal O_{D'}$.

source.place: Tags 0634 and 0635, lemma-conormal-algebra-functorial and lemma-conormal-algebra-functorial-flat; affine representative maps and restriction

proof.text: Take the jointly covering etale nodal charts of [lem-sfb-nodal-graph-cone-chart]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], their pullbacks cover $D'$ and remain etale; the pulled-back ambient nodal chart still has equation $uv-h'=0$. The chart lemma identifies the two graded algebras with the split-node algebras over $D_U$ and $D'_U$, preserving the homogeneous coordinate classes. On $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset D_U$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A'\subset D'_U$ above it, [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] identifies the source of the restricted comparison with $A'\otimes_A A[u,v]/(uv)$. The representative formula in Step 2 sends $r\otimes u^n$ to $ru^n$, $r\otimes v^n$ to $rv^n$, and $r\otimes1$ to $r$. This proves the asserted coordinate expression, including its agreement with the canonical comparison.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; agent comparison of the homogeneous coordinate representatives after arbitrary base change

proof.text: The bases supplied by the chart lemma make the last map invertible in every degree for every $A$-algebra $A'$: the inverse sends $r$ in degree zero to $r\otimes1$, and $ru^n+sv^n$ in degree $n>0$ to $r\otimes u^n+s\otimes v^n$. Products are respected since pure powers multiply as polynomials and mixed products vanish on both sides. Thus the pullback of $c_a$ to every covering chart is an isomorphism. These etale covering maps are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale]. Apply [lem-sc-flat-cover-module-isomorphism-reflection] degree by degree to conclude that $c_a$ is globally an isomorphism; the inverse of an invertible unital graded algebra map respects its algebra structure. This uses neither flatness of $a$ nor reducedness of $A$ or $A'$.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, split nodal chart calculation; Topologies Tag 022C and the existing flat-cover module reflection theorem

proof.text: For a second base change $b$, on a homogeneous representative an iterated pullback is generated by $([q]\otimes r)\otimes s$. Under tensor associativity the direct comparison sends it to $[q\otimes1]\,b^\sharp(r)s$, and the two successive comparisons send it to exactly the same class. Pure tensors generate each homogeneous module, so the maps agree; restriction gives the global composition law. For the identity base change $[q]\otimes r\mapsto r[q]$ is the tensor-unit identification. For a family isomorphism with affine ring map $h^\sharp$, the equality $(h^\sharp\otimes1)(q\otimes r)=h^\sharp(q)\otimes r$ shows that its square with $c_a$ commutes. These are identities of the representative maps already constructed, not choices of local bases.

source.place: Tag 0634, affine formula; agent identity, composition and family-isomorphism check on homogeneous pure tensors

proof.text: Apply [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality], clause 2, to the graded isomorphism $c_a$: it induces $\operatorname{Proj}_{D'}\mathcal G_{f'}\cong\operatorname{Proj}_{D'}(a_D^*\mathcal G_f)$. Apply [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] to $a_D$ and the quasi-coherent graded algebra $\mathcal G_f$ to identify the latter scheme with $(\operatorname{Proj}_D\mathcal G_f)\times_DD'$. Both maps are over $D'$, giving the required structural compatibility. The arbitrary-base-change lemma, rather than the flat-only clause of the functoriality node, is used here.

source.place: Tag 01O3, lemma-relative-proj-base-change; relative Proj under a degree-preserving graded algebra isomorphism

proof.text: Check the remaining Proj compatibilities on its standard homogeneous charts [def-nagata-affine-proj, def-nagata-relative-proj]. If $z$ is homogeneous of positive degree and $p/z^m$ has degree zero, the coefficientwise map is $r\otimes(p/z^m)\mapsto(r\otimes p)/(1\otimes z)^m$. For iterated pullback, both orders replace a coefficient $(r\otimes s)$ by $b^\sharp(r)s$ and replace $p,z$ by their successive pullbacks, by Step 5. For the identity they fix the fraction; applying a family isomorphism replaces numerator and denominator by their images and commutes with the same formula. Such fractions define the structure sheaf maps and these standard charts cover Proj; the restriction/gluing data in the relative-Proj definition therefore give the global identity, composition and family-isomorphism equalities.

source.place: Tag 01O3, lemma-relative-proj-base-change; agent check on degree-zero homogeneous fractions
